name: We’re Hiring!

pick.label: Pick a perk
pick.heading: Pick a perk and write the job ad
lead: Employers fight hard for good graduates, and their job ads promise everything: a fast-paced environment, a young dynamic team, free fruit on Tuesdays.
Choose a perk from the shelf, or invent your own, and build a graduate job ad around it. The perk can be generous, strange or slightly worrying. *Every perk has a catch.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a real HR strategy here, this is just for a bit of fun. If your ad would make a careers adviser cry, you’re doing it right.

shelf.head: Strange but true-ish
items: Lunch with the boss every week
Work from anywhere, even a beach

rows: Which perk from the shelf (or your own) are you offering?
What kind of company are you, and what kind of company do you pretend to be?
The first line graduates see. It has to beat 400 other ads.
Who exactly are you trying to attract? What do they want, and what are they tired of?
Every perk has one. What is it?
Where, and how do you make sure the right people see it?

values.firm: A very serious tax-advice firm in Mitte that would quite like you to think it’s a start-up.
values.headline: Wanted: junior tax adviser. Must be able to sleep on the job.
values.who: Graduates who have read the words ‘fast-paced environment’ in 400 job ads and now need a lie-down.
values.catch: There are two pods for 300 staff, and the partners book them from one till three every afternoon.
values.post: On TikTok, with a video of the managing partner trying to climb out of a nap pod. It takes him four minutes.
